title: PR-introduced compiler warning: unused `import gleam/option` in new draft integration test
evidence: Line 10 of the file is `import gleam/option` and it is the file's only occurrence of "option" (grep confirms). `gleam build` at the reviewed sha emits: "warning: Unused imported module ┌─ server/test/integration/draft_integration_test.gleam:10:1 │ 10 │ import gleam/option │ ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ This imported module is never used".
detail: New file added by this PR carries an unused import, adding a compiler warning to a previously warning-quiet build (CI does not fail on warnings, but the drift is PR-introduced).

title: draft_handler doc says "Errors are JSON" but DB-failure arms return text/plain 500
evidence: The doc comment on lookup_accepting_vacancy reads "/// Errors are JSON — these endpoints answer fetch/beacon calls, not browser navigations." yet its first arm is `Error(_) -> Error(wisp.internal_server_error())`, and wisp.internal_server_error() is `HttpResponse(500, [content_text], Text("Internal server error"))` with `const content_text = #("content-type", "text/plain")`. The same text/plain 500 is returned from handle_save_draft, handle_continue_link, and lookup_draft error arms.
detail: Internal doc/code mismatch: the JSON-error contract the module claims is not what the 500 paths return. Harmless (clients check status; codebase-wide precedent), but the comment overstates the contract.
recommended_fix: Either reword the comment to "errors are status-coded (JSON where the client reads a body)" or return wisp.json_response(json_ok(False), 500) from the 500 arms.
